target_customer: Non-technical workers and small businesses that want to automate repetitive browser tasks without code
problem: Repetitive browser work such as copying data between sites is manual, and classic RPA tools are heavy and enterprise priced.
business_model: Freemium SaaS Chrome extension with paid runtime hours and plans

founders.name: Yaseer Sheriff
prior_employers: Software consultancy run with co-founders (not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists engineering, computer science, automated theorem proving and computational biology; no institution named.

founders.name: Simon Williams
prior_employers: Own software engineering and web design consultancy for about 8 years
founders.background_notes: Moved from psychology into programming per the YC page.

founders.name: Alex Barlow
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

competitors.name: UiPath
competitors.what: Enterprise desktop RPA, named on the YC page as the example of a 10 billion dollar plus RPA business
competitors.traction_then: Described as a 10 billion dollar plus business

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension that records and replays clicks across arbitrary sites is standard engineering with fragile selectors as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Users build bots that lock them in modestly, but recording and replaying actions was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows UiPath or others copying or buying it; the site now integrates with Zapier, Make and n8n and positions with Claude.

market_need_then: YC description argues RPA had large potential outside the enterprise; the team came from an RPA consultancy that spun Axiom out, indicating customer demand for browser automation.

branding.domain_note: Uses axiom.ai, a .ai domain; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and functional, centered on bots, no-code and code

branding.community_and_virality: Self reported 300,000+ users and 800,000+ bots run on the company site; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Many unrelated companies share the Axiom name and no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Axiom.ai grew into a browser automation tool with a self reported 300,000 users and 800,000 bots run, backed by Y Combinator, and it keeps adding AI and Claude integrations. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is not verified beyond small aggregator figures, so the scale of the business is unclear.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights lists $250K over 4 rounds with a seed dated May 2021 (Abstraction Capital, SAP.iO Foundry, SFC Capital, YC, Jude Gomilla); EveryDev lists $330K; Signalbase pages claim $50M and $200M with no primary source and are disregarded. None are rounds because only aggregators state them. Aggregators also conflict on founding year (2018, 2019, 2020) and HQ (London vs Bristol). The YC page gives a 2019 founding year. Competitors beyond UiPath not found with dated sources. Outcome search found no news about Axiom.ai itself. Round recorded in the completeness pass rests on a single database (CB Insights seed 2021-05, no amount; Abstraction Capital confirmed by CB Insights page, SFC Capital not confirmed and omitted). Totals conflict: CB Insights 250K, Caplight 170K, EveryDev 330K to 460K; Signalbase 50M and 200M disregarded.
